summary: This work identifies that short-timescale waveform distortions break time-reflection symmetry in control pulses, creating an over-constrained optimization problem that limits fast CZ gate fidelity in superconducting qubits. A cyclic control strategy using parameter-space expansion with independent frequency detunings $\Delta_1$ and $\Delta_2$ restores controllability and achieves coherent error suppression from 0.27% to 0.12% without increasing gate duration.
motivation: Fast two-qubit gates are limited by a persistent speed-fidelity trade-off where reducing gate duration below ~50 ns increases coherent errors due to sub-10 ns distortions that conventional symmetric pulse protocols cannot suppress.
method: The authors demonstrate that short-timescale distortions break time-reflection symmetry ($H(t) = H(\tau - t)$), increasing cyclic evolution constraints from 2 to 3 in the $|11\rangle$–$|20\rangle$ subspace. The PSE-CZ protocol adds a third control degree of freedom by splitting the detuning profile into two segments ($\Delta_1 \neq \Delta_2$), enabling simultaneous satisfaction of leakage and conditional phase conditions on a 72-qubit superconducting processor.
result: Cross-entropy benchmarking on 20 qubit pairs at 50 ns gate duration shows mean fidelity improvement of 0.163%, with coherent error reduced from 0.27% to 0.12%, and leakage to $|20\rangle$ suppressed nearly threefold from 0.224% to 0.0756%, with consistent performance maintained across 30–50 ns durations.
